claim: On the unit-hopping cycle with two equal positive site defects the symmetric level is above the edge 2, and a second, antisymmetric level is above it exactly for V>2N/[d(N−d)], meeting it at equality. For V=λ/N and folded separation r_N=min(d_N,N−d_N)/N tending to ρ in (0,1/2], the limiting threshold is λ_c(ρ)=2/[ρ(1−ρ)]. At λ=λ_c(ρ), the second level is above 2 exactly when r_N>ρ, with no second above-edge level at ρ=1/2; on any above-edge subsequence at critical coupling its N²-scaled edge shift tends to zero. Positive scaled shifts are the squared roots of the stated two-channel equations.

integrity: The limiting secular equations specialize the known attractive point-interaction determinant on a continuum circle. The contribution assessed here concerns the finite lattice and its discrete-to-continuum scaling.
Originality is a best-knowledge assessment with residual historical-priority risk.
limitations: Equal positive defects only; nearest-neighbour cycle; unit hopping; one-particle Hamiltonian.
At the critical scaled coupling the count is controlled by the folded finite-size separation, with a fixed one-level above-edge count in the antipodal limit.
The numerical checker corroborates formulas but does not prove the infinite family or scaling limit.

title: Two-defect bound-state threshold and separation scaling on a finite cycle
